newsitem.title: FRANCE: Drought cuts Algeria's harvest to 1.05 mln T - APS.
newsitem.headline: Drought cuts Algeria's harvest to 1.05 mln T - APS.

text.p: Algeria's cereal harvest will fall to a 20-year low of about 1.05 million tonnes in the 1996/97 season from a record of 4.9 million tonnes the previous season, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Sunday.
Drought scorched 65 percent of the country's 3.5 million hectares (8.75 million acres) sown with cereals, said APS quoting Agriculture Minister Belahouadjeb Benalia.
It said the minister was addressing officials gathering in Algiers to assess the impact of drought on the farmers.
"This situation will directly result in a cut in output. The reduced harvest will amount to an estimated 10.5 million quintals (1.05 million tonnes) or the lowest production in 20 years," said APS.
Harvesting in the vast country, Africa's second largest, starts in the southern areas in late May and in June in other areas, being completed early in August.
The government earmarked 3.5 billion dinars ($62.5 million) for drought-sticken farmers who had paid an insurance policy for fields.
The authorities promised soft loans for farmers who were not covered by insurance, APS said.
Officials have said that only one-third of about one million Algerian farmers subscribed to insurance schemes.
Algeria, one of the world's leading importers of durum wheat, harvested 4.9 million tonnes in the 1995/1996 season thanks mainly to good rains.
